aria: Animated recap of the Warriors' 129 to 110 win over the Kings: De'Anthony Melton's eighth three with 2:05 left that made it 123 to 102, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Melton's 24 points, the top scorers, how the Warriors won, and the next game.

figure.label: De'Anthony Melton, listed 6-2, 201 lb (Basketball-Reference); no sourced wingspan

notes: Box score from Hoops Nightly's game page for the Warriors' 129–110 win over the Kings on Nov 25, 2026: all 129 Golden State points and all 110 Sacramento points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (49 of 92, 20 of 44 from three, 11 of 14 FT for Golden State; 41 of 87, 14 of 40, 14 of 19 for Sacramento), rebounds (40–39), assists (37–31), steals (9–6) and blocks (7–2); every player's points also match the San Francisco Chronicle box score. The final and the quarter scores (44–28–29–28 to 19–34–36–21) match FOX Sports and the San Francisco Chronicle; 72–53 at the half and 101–89 after three are in the FOX Sports play-by-play. Points off turnovers (26–11) and fast-break points (9–12) are on FOX Sports and Hoops Nightly; bench points (61–19) on Hoops Nightly, and the AP and NBC Sports Bay Area call the 61 a season best. Golden State's biggest lead, 29, is in Hoops Nightly, Field Level Media and the San Francisco Chronicle; Sacramento's 3 is in Hoops Nightly (10–7 in the first quarter, FOX Sports play-by-play). Records are from the AP and the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Golden State scored 44 in the first quarter, its most in any period this season (AP), on a 21–2 run (Field Level Media). Sacramento cut it to 82–78 with a 25–10 run in the third (Field Level Media) and to 85–81 on Emanuel Sharp's three with 4:34 left in it; Will Richard answered with a baseline three (AP), and the Kings never got within 8 in the fourth (Field Level Media). Gui Santos scored a season-high 22 (San Francisco Chronicle). Stephen Curry (oblique) and Jimmy Butler did not play (San Francisco Chronicle). The Warriors have won eight straight at home (Fastbreak Journal) and are 2–1 in the NBA Cup; they need a win at Portland on Friday to have a chance to advance (AP; Field Level Media). Sacramento hosts Minnesota on Sunday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of De'Anthony Melton's three with 2:05 left that made it 123–102, assisted by Brandin Podziemski: the FOX Sports play-by-play has it at 2:05 for 123–102, and it was his eighth three of the night (four in the first quarter, two in the second, two in the fourth), which tied his career high (AP; StatMuse: his other eight-three game was Dec 9, 2022). So the board's Warriors +18 to +21 is 120–102 to 123–102. The defender isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Golden State Warriors or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Melton's listed 6-foot-2 and 201 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia lists 199), with arms at the default length because no wingspan is reported, in the Warriors' home kit with No. 8 (Wikipedia); he has no approved look yet, so he is drawn with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
